info.title: Logic in everyday rules
info.text: Nearly every automatic device hides a logic expression: a boiler, a lift, a car alarm. Reading the rule and underlining the words and, or and not is most of the work.

info.title: Real alarms
info.text: Burglar alarms really are built from logic like this, often with extra inputs for doors, windows and a timer.

info.title: Fail-safe design
info.text: Emergency stops are usually wired so that a broken wire also stops the machine. Safety engineers call this fail-safe design.

info.title: Programmable logic
info.text: Factories use programmable logic controllers (PLCs), which are programmed with logic diagrams very like the ones you're drawing.

info.title: Test everything
info.text: A truth table tests every possible combination, so engineers can prove a safety circuit will always behave correctly.

info.title: Simplify it
info.text: Different circuits can give identical truth tables. Engineers choose the one with the fewest gates, because it's cheaper and faster.
